questions.question: In mobile-first CSS, what role do `min-width` media queries play?
options: They remove styles as the screen gets smaller
They add or override the unconditional base (mobile) styles as more viewport width becomes available
They only apply to print stylesheets
They have the same effect as max-width queries
questions.explanation: Mobile-first means small-screen styles are the default; min-width queries progressively layer on more complex layout for larger viewports.

questions.question: What goes wrong on mobile browsers if the viewport meta tag is omitted?
options: The browser renders at a desktop-width virtual viewport (e.g. 980px) and zooms out, so media query breakpoints fire at the wrong actual widths
The page fails to load entirely
questions.explanation: Without the viewport meta tag, mobile browsers assume a wide desktop viewport and scale the page down, which breaks the relationship between CSS breakpoints and the device's real width.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to choose breakpoints?
options: Copy a fixed list of exact device widths from a popular phone/tablet model list
Let your own content and layout tell you where it starts to look cramped or sparse, rather than targeting specific device widths
Breakpoints should never be customized per project
Always use exactly 3 breakpoints regardless of the design
questions.explanation: Device-width lists go stale as new devices ship; designing breakpoints around where your actual content breaks is a more durable approach.

questions.question: What problem do container queries solve that media queries cannot?
options: They let a reusable component adapt based on the size of its actual container (e.g. a sidebar vs a main column), not just the overall viewport
They replace the need for any CSS selectors
They only work on mobile devices
questions.explanation: A component dropped into differently-sized containers on the same page can't distinguish them via viewport-based media queries, but container queries respond directly to the container's own size.
